harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as a DHCP server on the private eth1/enp8s0 network (10.50.50.0/24) shared with node2/node3, and configured node2/node3 (RHEL9) to obtain their address on that network via DHCP instead of static assignment, implemented entirely via an Ansible playbook run from node4 (the cluster's only Ansible-equipped node, used as control_node). Verified leases issued and held by node2/node3, then performed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol across all four managed nodes, confirming changed boot IDs and full post-restart recovery on each.
actions_performed: Surveyed all 4 nodes: node1 is VyOS (eth0 on shared cluster net; eth1/enp8s0 unconfigured private net shared with node2/node3), node2/node3 are RHEL9 with enp8s0 already NetworkManager ipv4.method=auto but unaddressed, node4 is Ubuntu 24.04 with Ansible pre-installed (the control_node)

Wired passwordless SSH from node4 to node1 (vyos user, via VyOS 'set system login user vyos authentication public-keys'), and to node2/node3 (root, via authorized_keys), using the cluster's CLUSTER_SSH_PRIVKEY/PUBKEY
Installed the vyos.vyos Ansible collection on node4; community.general was already present

Wrote /root/ansible/dhcp-lan/{inventory.ini,dhcp-lan.yml} on node4: play 1 sets node1's eth1 static address (10.50.50.254/24) and a Kea DHCP-server shared-network 'LAN' (subnet 10.50.50.0/24, range .100-.200, default-router/name-server) via vyos_config; play 2 ensures node2/node3's private NIC NetworkManager profile uses method4: auto via community.general.nmcli
Debugged VyOS's dhcp-server@11 schema (requires subnet-id and a nested 'option' node) by testing manually on node1 first, then encoded the corrected syntax into the playbook
Ran the playbook from node4 against node1/node2/node3; confirmed node2 leased 10.50.50.101 and node3 leased 10.50.50.100 from node1's Kea server, verified via dhcp4-leases.csv on node1
Captured a healthy baseline (boot_id, DHCP/lease state) on all 4 nodes, then restarted node1, node2, node3, and node4 one at a time, polling each until reachable and confirming its boot_id changed

After each restart verified recovery: node1's DHCP config/leases persisted and Kea running; node2/node3 re-obtained their DHCP leases and could ping node1; node4's Ansible files intact and a full playbook re-run after all restarts was fully idempotent (0 changes)

evidence.requirement: node1 configured as DHCP server on private network shared with node2/node3 (via Ansible)
evidence.summary: Manual syntax validation on node1 followed by successful idempotent Ansible playbook run configuring eth1 address and Kea DHCP-server subnet; Kea process confirmed running

evidence.requirement: node2/node3 configured to obtain address via DHCP from node1 rather than static (via Ansible)
evidence.summary: Ansible nmcli task applied method4:auto to node2/node3's private NIC; both nodes shown holding DHCP leases 10.50.50.101 and 10.50.50.100 respectively

evidence.requirement: DHCP server actually issuing leases to node2/node3
evidence.summary: node1's Kea dhcp4-leases.csv lists leases for node2 (10.50.50.101) and node3 (10.50.50.100) by hostname and MAC

evidence.requirement: node1 healthy baseline and restart recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id/Kea state captured; reboot acknowledged before disconnect; boot_id changed after reboot (2eb8b6e8...->5e3ececb...); post-restart eth1 address, Kea process, saved dhcp-server config, and prior leases all confirmed intact

evidence.requirement: node2 healthy baseline and restart recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id/lease captured; reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed (6aa805ba...->7e1147d2...); post-restart DHCP lease 10.50.50.101 re-obtained and node1 reachable via ping

evidence.requirement: node3 healthy baseline and restart recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id/lease captured; reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed (377b5195...->e6576dbf...); post-restart DHCP lease 10.50.50.100 re-obtained and node1 reachable via ping

evidence.requirement: node4 (control node) healthy baseline and restart recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id and Ansible files captured; reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed (6fd57414...->a4a2c369...); post-restart Ansible files intact and a full playbook re-run against all managed nodes succeeded fully idempotently (0 changes across node1/node2/node3)
